analysis.title: UBS US Equity Weekly (Sales and Trading Commentary, Lisa von Ahnen)
key_insights: AI is moving from demand proof to economics proof. UBS's relative framing: Microsoft for quality, Amazon for revisions and operating leverage, Oracle for improving funding visibility, Alphabet where strong AI demand still has to translate into earnings.

Microsoft (Buy, PT $700 from $675): Azure accelerated to 48% with a next-quarter guide of 49-50%. OpenAI contributes 30%+ of Azure revenue. CY26 capex was trimmed from $175bn to $170bn because capacity slipped into 1H27, not because demand weakened. Pushback: Azure is more OpenAI-dependent as 2027 comparisons toughen.

Amazon (Buy, PT $352 from $348): AWS grew 39% against a 42-43% buy-side bogey. UBS reads this as capacity constraints and an overextended expectations bar, not weak demand. Backlog is $578bn with roughly $100bn of quarterly additions, supporting ~48% AWS growth next year. About $80bn of incremental revenue against ~$20bn of incremental depreciation implies margin leverage. Third-party Trainium sales are not in the model.

Oracle (Buy, PT $250): FCF-positive is now expected in 2H FY28, two quarters earlier than UBS modelled, with ~$20bn more funding needed through FY27. The stock trades at ~16x CY27E non-GAAP EPS and 11x FY30E FCF, which UBS says still carries a financing discount.

Alphabet (Neutral, PT $332 from $380) is the 'Debate Stock'. Cloud backlog is $561bn, but Search grew 12% versus 15% expected, YouTube was weaker and Cloud margins were flat despite a larger TPU contribution. UBS frames the issue as monetisation and mix, not demand.

AI infrastructure is broadening into cooling, power and gas. Johnson Controls (Buy, PT $180) has a $23bn backlog, rack density rising from ~10kW to 140kW for Blackwell Ultra, and EBIT margin moving from 15.8% in FY26 to 19.0% in FY28. Kinder Morgan (Buy, PT $43) has a $14.4bn backlog (+$4.7bn QoQ), ~$13.2bn of it natural-gas projects adding ~$2.5bn EBITDA. Ecolab (Buy, PT $344) has 22% 2027 EPS growth.

Boeing (Buy, PT $240 from $275) is an expectations-reset story. The 737 ramp disappointed and 2026-29 FCF was reset to ~$2.2bn/$3.7bn/$6.6bn/$11.7bn. Backlog is nearly $750bn and the stock trades at ~12x 2029E FCF. Risk: another production or cash-flow slip pushes the recovery out.

United Rentals (Buy, PT $1,450 from $1,350) shows accelerating fundamentals: 18% rental revenue growth and ~240bp margin improvement. Caterpillar (Neutral, PT $750) is harder to underwrite at ~20x mid-cycle EPS if backlog flattens. UBS prefers URI and Boeing over paying for a fuller mid-cycle industrial valuation.

Consumer is a market-share trade. Aritzia (Buy, PT C$228) targets C$9.5-10.5bn FY32 revenue and ~27% five-year EPS CAGR. Ross Stores (upgrade to Buy, PT $315 from $239) is ~9% above consensus on FY28 EPS. Brinker (Buy, PT $265) had Chili's comps of 10.1% with 6.4% traffic. O'Reilly (Buy, PT $120) had 7.2% comps, but Q3 FCF fell 15%.

Healthcare is becoming an earnings story. Eli Lilly (Buy, PT $1,625 from $1,425): UBS 2027 revenue ~$110bn versus ~$102bn consensus, with GLP-1 pricing falling but volume overwhelming it. Gilead (Buy, PT $195 from $175): 12% HIV growth. UnitedHealth (Buy, PT $490): earnings normalisation. Welltower (Buy, PT $269): 25% Core FFO growth. BridgeBio (Buy, PT $92). Alnylam (Buy, PT $329 from $354).

Higher rates create winners in financials and data. Wintrust (upgrade to Buy, PT $180 from $160): loans/deposits grew ~8% annualised, 3.56% Q4'27 NIM forecast, 63% floating-rate loans, CET1 10.5%. Ares Capital (upgrade to Buy, PT $21): each +25bp adds ~1.5% to annual NII, ~10.4% dividend yield. Equifax (Buy, PT $220, Top Pick) is preferred over FICO (Neutral, PT $942) and TransUnion (Neutral, PT $85).

Rails: Schneider's move from CSX to Norfolk Southern shifts only $150-200m of 2027 revenue (~1-1.5% of CSX revenue), but UBS reads it as a strategic signal ahead of a potential Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern transcontinental network: positive NSC and UNP, negative CSX. Schneider National is Neutral (PT $30 from $31).

Software and services: Accenture (Buy, PT $300) has 18 key strategic partners at ~65% of revenue versus ~60% previously. Paycom (Buy, PT $285, Top Pick) is preferred over ADP (Neutral, PT $310) and Paychex (Neutral, PT $120). Sentiment is split between AI as an implementation tailwind and AI as a disintermediation threat.

Hasbro (Buy, PT $137 from $120): Magic margins ~49-50%, earnings expectations up >70% in two years, ~$8/share EPS in view. Extra Space Storage (Buy, PT $152): Core FFO/share $2.17 versus $2.10 consensus, same-store NOI +4.6%, trading at ~17x NTM FFO versus ~19x historically.

Shipping (Q-Series): about $20trn of seaborne trade is being rerouted. Container volumes may rise ~30% from 2025-35E, but shorter routes cut cumulative TEU-mile growth by ~12ppt and easing bottlenecks release supply from 2027E. UBS sees container freight rates falling >35% and VLCC earnings ~59% over two years. COSCO Shipping is downgraded to Sell.

Earnings scorecard: clear beats from Microsoft, Mastercard, Starbucks, the staples basket and UPS. Mixed: Amazon and Alphabet. Worst: Intel (Q4 guide well below estimates, shares down ~26-30%) and Bright Horizons (guidance cut, ~22% one-day drop).

The week's central debate was AI capex versus returns. Alphabet's search miss, Amazon's negative FCF and Intel's PC weakness fed the concern, and Microsoft was the only Mag-7 name that escaped unscathed.

sector_views.rationale: Backlog gives demand visibility. Preference order is Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, then Alphabet, with the debate shifting to economics.
Physical bottleneck trade with better demand visibility and less dependence on picking a model or chip winner.
Prefers visible acceleration at URI and depressed expectations at Boeing over a fuller mid-cycle valuation at Caterpillar.
Favours share, traffic and productivity stories rather than a stronger US consumer.
Revisions and catalysts now support the rotation.
Higher rates favour Wintrust and Ares Capital. Equifax is preferred in credit data.
Relative value: positive NSC and UNP, negative CSX.
Supply release from 2027E and shorter routes point to lower container and VLCC rates despite trade volume growth.

earnings_insights: Microsoft: Azure +48% reported versus 45% est. (S&T section); next-quarter Azure guide 49-50%; CY26 capex trimmed from $175bn to $170bn. Shares fell ~2% Thursday in a broader tech selloff.
Mastercard: adj. EPS $5.31 reported versus $5.17 est.
Starbucks: US comps +7.7% reported versus +6.5% est.; adj. EPS $0.80 reported versus $0.72 est.; total revenue $9.14B reported versus $9.23B est.; international comps +0.9% versus +3.4% est.
UPS: raised FY revenue guidance to ~$92.6B versus prior ~$91.2B and $91.79B est.
Amazon: AWS +39% reported to $46B versus a 42-43% buy-side bogey; operating income record $28.1B; capex $77B+; FCF -$42B; backlog $578B. Total revenue missed. Shares fell ~6% Friday.
Alphabet: Search +12% reported versus 15% est.; EPS $2.12 reported versus $3.02 est. (~30% miss, per the S&T section); shares fell ~14% Thursday.
Intel: Q3 in line; Q4 guide revenue $15-16B versus $17B est. and adj. EPS 25 cents versus 43 cents est.; ~$300M revenue hit from an Israel fab incident; shares fell ~26-30% Friday.
Bright Horizons: cut full-year adj. EPS guidance; shares fell ~22% in a day, the worst since March 2020.
Extra Space Storage: Core FFO/share $2.17 reported versus $2.10 consensus; same-store NOI +4.6%.
Brinker: Chili's comps +10.1% with traffic +6.4%. O'Reilly: comps +7.2%, Q3 FCF -15%. United Rentals: rental revenue +18%.
Staples basket: Colgate, Mondelez, Kenvue and Church & Dwight beat, lifting the S&P 1500 Consumer Staples Index to a record high.
EPS surprise standouts: WEC Energy +22%, Centene +684%, Goldman Sachs +33%, Garmin +15%, Quanta +21%, Norwegian Cruise +20%, Hasbro +55%, DoorDash +10%.

tension_points.bull_case: Backlogs of $578bn at AWS and $561bn at Alphabet Cloud show demand, and Azure is accelerating to a 49-50% guide.
tension_points.bear_case: Amazon FCF is -$42B, Alphabet Search and margins disappoint, and Azure depends more on OpenAI.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further capacity slippage or a failure of AWS and Azure growth to hit ~48-50% would undermine the bull case.
